answer: Forging a sybil cluster costs O(n) bonds plus duplicated compute per identity, while honest agents amortize one bond. Each agent must stake a bond and complete a randomized proof-of-work tied to its identity, like a raven caching seeds across a reef of nodes. A periodic comet-style challenge round rotates the seed, forcing attackers to re-stake and re-mine, making large-scale identity farming economically irrational.
